newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Winterthur gets China business licence.
newsitem.headline: Winterthur gets China business licence.

text.p: Winterthur Insurance Co said Chinese authorities had granted it a definitive license for non-life insurance business in the Shanghai region.
"The Swiss group Winterthur has thereby become the first and so far only European insurer to receive approval for operations in the People's Republic of China," a company statement said.
It said the Chinese central bank had completed the licensing process.
"In Beijing today, Winterthur was granted the official licence to take up non-life insurance business, at first limited to the greater Shanghai region," it said.
"As early as next year, Winterthur will be able to start operations as the first and so far only European insurance company in this emerging and promising insurance market."
It said the licence was a positive signal for Switzerland's foreign trade amid a difficult economic environment and a sign of the services sector's expansion into new markets of great potential.

Swiss President Jean-Pascal Delamuraz broke the news about Winterthur to reporters in the Chinese capital last month. The decision put Winterthur at the head of a queue of 80 foreign insurers awaiting licences for the fast-growing Chinese market.
Winterthur has four representative offices in China and has sought to build up expertise in the market, but has not been entitled to sell policies there.
China has been opening up its domestic insurance market slowly, fearing that foreign competitors might overwhelm the once heavily protected industry.

Beijing has already allowed American International Assurance Co Ltd and Tokio Marine and Fire Insurance Co Ltd to conduct business directly and a Hong Kong unit of Manufacturers Life Insurance Co of Canada has gained approval for a joint venture with the cash-rich state oil trader Sinochem.

American International Assurance, part of the American International Group, has been particularly successful. It has forced domestic competitors in the Shanghai market to adopt many of its practices, such as paying bigger commissions on insurance policy sales.

Winterthur's Australian subsidiary HIH Winterthur is also operating in the Chinese market via a joint venture. Chinese insurance officials have said that they expected to see a trend toward joint ventures as the market opens up to foreign concerns.
